question: Does the domain gate decide whether a passage is about mating, or whether it contains a keyword the gate recognises?
method: Each case states one claim twice. `keyed` contains a word inside a decisive relational-outcome frame; `plain` says the same thing without one. A gate reasoning about subject matter gives both members the same verdict.
provenance: Authored, not scraped. The gap was found over lab-corpus/sources, which is gitignored third-party text (md/RERUN.md 1) and whose excerpts the threshold sweep caps hard; these carry the structure the corpus demonstrated without reproducing it.
ratchet: knownSplits is a defect count and may only be LOWERED. A change that raises it has widened the register gap.

keyed.text: Social conventions around courtship were rewritten without anyone voting on the change.

plain.text: Social conventions around pairing up were rewritten without anyone voting on the change.

keyed.text: The stories a culture tells about romance shape what its young people believe they are owed.

plain.text: The stories a culture tells about intimacy shape what its young people believe they are owed.

keyed.text: Conditioning teaches women to want the qualities their mothers were taught to reject.

plain.text: Conditioning teaches a generation to prize the qualities their mothers were taught to reject.

keyed.text: The culture treats what women want as the default setting nobody argues about.

plain.text: The culture treats one sex’s preferences as the default setting nobody argues about.

keyed.text: Media that ridiculed masculinity for a generation changed who young women date.

plain.text: Media that ridiculed masculinity for a generation changed how young men present themselves.

keyed.text: Family law encodes one sex’s interests as the neutral baseline when a marriage ends.

plain.text: Family law encodes one sex’s interests as the neutral baseline when a household dissolves.

keyed.text: The operative frame in which men and women date is culturally manufactured, not natural.

plain.text: The operative frame in which the sexes encounter each other is culturally manufactured, not natural.

keyed.text: The script for a good life was rewritten, and it no longer has marriage at the centre.

plain.text: The script for a good life was rewritten, and it no longer has the household at the centre.

adopted.ruling: Option 1 of md/lab-gate-cultural-register.md, adopted on Jason's ruling 2026-07-30.
adopted.effect: Splits 6 -> 3. Benchmark domainRecall held at 1.000, ignorePrecision 1.000, junkRecall 0.821 -> 0.833. No expected-ignore case is retained because of the new frame.
adopted.residual: The 3 remaining splits share one cause and it is NOT the new frame: it fires at 2.5 on all three, but HUMAN_PARTICIPANT_FRAMES does not recognise `anyone`, `a generation`, `mothers` or `the sexes`, so no participant is detected and option 1 requires one. Widening the participant vocabulary is a separate, narrower ruling and was deliberately not taken here, because it would change what option 1 was measured to be.
